title: Ajitsuke Tamago (Marinated eggs for Ramen)
description: Soft-boiled, marinated eggs for Japanese cooking (Ramen, mostly).

equipment.name: Fine needle or thumbtack
equipment.note: For piercing the eggshell to release trapped air.

stages.label: Preparation
stages.description: Prepare the marinade and eggs before cooking.

steps.instruction: Whisk together the water, {1} sake, {2} soy sauce, {3} mirin, and {4} sugar until dissolved.
For each of the {1}, use your thumbtack or needle to poke a small hole at the base of the fat end of the egg.
steps.hint: This releases the air, preventing air pockets from forming.

stages.label: Cooking & Marinating
stages.description: Soft-boil the eggs, then marinate them in the prepared sauce.

steps.instruction: Pour the boiled kettle water into the saucepan on a high heat.
Once it is boiling, reduce to a bare simmer.
Using the slotted spoon, add each of the {1} one at a time.
Switch off the heat. Use the slotted spoon to remove each egg.
Carefully peel the eggs under running cold water.
Transfer the eggs to your bowl. Pour marinade in until the eggs are just barely covered, or floating.
Place a double layer of kitchen roll over the eggs. Press down until completely saturated in the liquid.
steps.hint: This ensures that even if the eggs float, they will be fully submerged in the marinade.

steps.instruction: Refrigerate for 4-12 hours. Never longer than 12 hours. When finished marinating, move the eggs to a container where they will keep in the fridge for 3 days.
